reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: The word-event, genealogy, and date notice closes before first-person sweeping judgment speech begins at Zeph.1.2.
reviews.counterevidence: The superscription governs the whole book and therefore still requires book-level context.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: Repeated sweeping verbs expand across humans and creatures and close with a speech formula before the geographic narrowing to Judah and Jerusalem at Zeph.1.4.
reviews.counterevidence: Cutting-off language continues into 1:4, but the geographic and object narrowing is the stronger surface seam.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: The hand-against-Judah-and-Jerusalem declaration introduces coordinated cultic allegiance, withdrawal, and failure-to-seek accusations; the hush imperative restarts the discourse at Zeph.1.7.
reviews.counterevidence: The catalogue moves from named practices to the broader failure to seek, creating internal variation but not a stronger surface boundary.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: The hush command and near-day declaration develop through prepared sacrifice and punishment; a WLC-family samekh follows Zeph.1.9 before the city soundscape begins at 1:10.
reviews.counterevidence: Day language continues throughout 1:10-18, requiring the larger day-complex parent.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: The in-that-day city soundscape moves through merchant lament and lamp search to the complacency saying and property reversal; the great-day refrain restarts at Zeph.1.14.
reviews.counterevidence: The move from public soundscape to private lamp search at 1:12 is a recoverable internal turn.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: The great-day restart and repeated day register escalate through battle, darkness, alarm, distress, blood, fire, and terminal closure; a WLC-family samekh follows Zeph.1.18.
reviews.counterevidence: The consequences in 1:17-18 could be treated as a dependent concluding stanza.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: Repeated gathering, before, and seek expressions culminate in possible concealment; the causal nations rationale begins at Zeph.2.4.
reviews.counterevidence: The terse wording and addressee scope of 2:1 remain translation-sensitive without changing the surface boundary.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: The causal four-city catalogue at Zeph.2.4 prepares the coast woe, desolation, and Judah-remnant reversal through 2:7; Zeph.2.8 begins a new first-person hearing oracle concerning Moab and Ammon.
reviews.counterevidence: The WLC-family samekh after 2:4 and fresh woe at 2:5 support a real dependent child seam; that seam is preserved as dissent rather than erased.

challenges.claim: The WLC-family samekh after 2:4 and fresh woe at 2:5 support a real dependent child seam; that seam is preserved as dissent rather than erased.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Evaluate the preserved alternative: Zeph.2.4-Zeph.2.4 plus Zeph.2.5-Zeph.2.7; Zeph.2.4-Zeph.2.11
challenges.counterevidence: Causal continuity and the coastland movement from city loss through desolation to remnant reversal outweigh the paragraph pressure to expose Zeph.2.4 independently.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: First-person hearing, oath, Sodom-and-Gomorrah comparison, remnant inheritance, pride rationale, and widened worship horizon form one oracle before the direct Cush address at Zeph.2.12.
reviews.counterevidence: Zeph.2.11 broadens beyond Moab and Ammon and could be retained as a dependent concluding horizon child.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: The second-person Cush address and complete sword clause create a compact compass-cycle turn; the northward Assyria movement begins at Zeph.2.13.
reviews.counterevidence: Its brevity makes isolated retrieval risky; it must retain nations-cycle hydration and cannot authorize historical or ethnic conclusions.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: The northern turn, desolation, animal habitation, exposed architecture, proud self-speech, and passerby response close together before the WLC-family samekh after Zeph.2.15.
reviews.counterevidence: The city self-speech at 2:15 is a strong internal rhetorical turn.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: The city woe, four failures, predatory leaders, treacherous prophets, profaning priests, and righteous-Yahweh contrast form one movement before the destroyed-nations example at Zeph.3.6.
reviews.counterevidence: Zeph.3.5 changes from accusation to divine contrast and remains a recoverable dependent turn.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: The destroyed-nations example leads to the quoted correction summons and failed response; therefore-wait-for-me pivots at Zeph.3.8.
reviews.counterevidence: Pronoun and causal scope link the movement backward to the city woe and forward to the therefore clause.

challenges.claim: Pronoun and causal scope link the movement backward to the city woe and forward to the therefore clause.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Evaluate the preserved alternative: Attach Zeph.3.6-Zeph.3.7 wholly to Zeph.3.1-Zeph.3.5; Attach Zeph.3.6-Zeph.3.7 wholly to Zeph.3.8-Zeph.3.13; Separate the correction quotation from its failed response
challenges.counterevidence: Example, expected correction, and failed response form a complete warning-response movement before the inferential pivot.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: Therefore-wait-for-me gathers the preceding failed correction into a judicial assembly declaration; the for-then expression at Zeph.3.9 turns from judgment to purified speech and service.
reviews.counterevidence: The verse depends strongly on both neighboring movements and must never surface without the Zeph.3.8-Zeph.3.13 parent.

challenges.claim: The verse depends strongly on both neighboring movements and must never surface without the Zeph.3.8-Zeph.3.13 parent.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Evaluate the preserved alternative: Zeph.3.6-Zeph.3.8; Zeph.3.8-Zeph.3.13
challenges.counterevidence: Its inferential opening, wait summons, assembly language, and judgment culmination make it a recoverable pivot, while the causal-temporal turn at 3:9 begins the resulting promise movement.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: The for-then turn develops purified speech, joint service, and dispersed worshipers through Zeph.3.10; the in-that-day formula and renewed feminine-singular city address begin a distinct remnant movement at 3:11.
reviews.counterevidence: Purification, pride removal, and remnant formation remain one larger restoration sequence, so the canonical lane's whole Zeph.3.9-Zeph.3.13 surface remains a defensible dissent.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: The in-that-day formula and city address introduce removal of pride and the remaining humble people; truthful speech, rest, and safety close before the WLC-family samekh after Zeph.3.13.
reviews.counterevidence: The unit is causally continuous with purification in 3:9-10 and cannot be treated as an independent identity proposition.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: Song imperatives at Zeph.3.14 develop through removed judgments, royal presence, the fear-not reassurance reported at 3:16, saving presence, and divine rejoicing through 3:17.
reviews.counterevidence: The in-that-day report at 3:16 is a genuine internal speech seam and supports the canonical lane's proposed child division.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: The difficult first-person collection language at Zeph.3.18 proceeds into explicit rescue, gathering, praise, and return language and closes with the says-Yahweh formula at 3:20.
reviews.counterevidence: The syntax and subject scope of Zeph.3.18 are difficult and may connect backward to the song or its festal setting; this lowers confidence but does not presently require a boundary hold.

challenges.claim: The syntax and subject scope of Zeph.3.18 are difficult and may connect backward to the song or its festal setting; this lowers confidence but does not presently require a boundary hold.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Evaluate the preserved alternative: Attach Zeph.3.18 to Zeph.3.14-Zeph.3.17; Zeph.3.19-Zeph.3.20; Detach Zeph.3.20 as an isolated promise
challenges.counterevidence: First-person collection, rescue, gathering, praise, return, and the terminal speech formula support a closing restoration movement while avoiding a preferred resolution of Zeph.3.18's syntax.
